subject.title: TUI: Support Shift+Enter for newline (Enter to send)

question: Should OpenClaw resolve the remaining work with terminal-aware TUI documentation/help only, or introduce and own a persistent configurable send/newline keybinding preference?
rationale: The current dependency already provides the baseline newline behavior, while exposing a preference would add a durable config and UX contract that source inspection cannot choose safely.

options.title: Document existing behavior
options.body: Add TUI help and docs for Pi's modified-Enter newline shortcuts, their terminal-dependent nature, and the available fallback; do not add a new config surface.

options.title: Own a keybinding preference
options.body: Design a canonical TUI configuration contract that wires a selected send/newline mapping into the editor, with documented defaults and focused compatibility tests.

options.title: Defer the preference
options.body: Keep the current inherited behavior and defer both expanded documentation and configuration until TUI input ergonomics are planned as a broader product slice.

recommendation.title: Document existing behavior
recommendation.body: Add TUI help and docs for Pi's modified-Enter newline shortcuts, their terminal-dependent nature, and the available fallback; do not add a new config surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature and current documentation history both point to steipete as the strongest available owner for the TUI product-boundary decision.
